subject: Mutual action plan: throughput budget & fallback routing for Meridian
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@meridian.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Mutual action plan: throughput budget & fallback routing for Meridian

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. As discussed, we want to capture a short mutual action plan so our CS + engineering teams can kick off the cost/perf tuning work for your inference integration. High-level items below; please confirm or correct and add anything I missed.

1) Peak traffic and latency targets
   - Stated peak: ~120 requests/sec (inference requests) with average payloads of ~520 tokens.
   - Meridian SLO: P95 <= 300ms for inference (real-time features).

2) Cost / quantization guardrails
   - We propose a primary 8-bit quantized profile for the production variant (int8 dynamic where supported).
   - Fallback to an FP16 or mixed-precision variant only for tail latency/accuracy-sensitive flows.

3) Batching and latency windows
   - Recommend adaptive batching with a 50ms batching window for low-latency routes, and 200ms for offline/async flows.

4) KV/prefix caching
   - Acceptable TTLs for prefix cache? We propose 10m for session-level caches and 30m for model-prefetch caches.

5) Routing / fallback policy
   - Policy: route by latency-first (keep P95 target), cost-aware second. If capacity constrained, fallback to cheaper quantized variant or redirect to a higher-latency batch endpoint.

6) Canary plan + signoffs
   - We’ll run a 48-hour canary on Dedicated pool with 5% traffic, then 20% for 24 hours before full cutover.

Next actions: we’ll prepare a proposed inference profile and a short runbook for the canary. Can you confirm the peak requests/sec and whether the 10m/30m TTLs are acceptable? I attached a quick MAP sheet (meridian_map_v1.xlsx).

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Samira Khan <samira@meridian.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Meridian DevOps <infra@meridian.ai>, Alex Liu <alex.liu@meridian.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: throughput budget & fallback routing for Meridian

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the summary. Quick answers inline:

1) Peak traffic: recent load tests show sustained 110–130 rps; spiky bursts to ~180 rps for short periods during business hours.
2) P95 target: yes, 300ms is what the product team requires for the real-time endpoint. We can accept slightly higher latency for background endpoints.
3) Quantization: 8-bit primary sounds fine. We will need to validate approximate-answer quality on a 1k prompt subset — we can share labeled samples.
4) TTLs: 10m session, 30m prefetch both acceptable.

Two requests from our side:
- Please include the exact model variants (names/ids) you recommend for primary vs fallback in the proposal so our procurement team can pre-approve them.
- A short canary runbook (list of checks and abort criteria) — Alex will run the canary.

I attached our infra inventory.

Best,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform — Meridian AI
samira@meridian.ai
Attachment: meridian_infra_inventory.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@meridian.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: throughput budget & fallback routing for Meridian

Samira — thanks, that's helpful. Attached is a short proposal (inference_profile_proposal.md) with concrete suggestions. Summary of changes from the MAP:

- Model variants
  - Primary: redwood/compat-v2-int8 (latency-optimized int8 runtime).
  - Fallback: redwood/compat-v2-fp16 (higher-accuracy, higher-cost).

- Quantization profile note
  - Primary int8 will use dynamic quantization with per-channel scales for attention weights; we recommend a small accuracy validation set (you offered 1k samples). If accuracy regression > 2.5% on top-K metrics, we fail to promote and iterate.

- Batching windows
  - Live low-latency route: 40–60ms adaptive window with priority queuing for priority sessions.
  - Background route: 150–250ms window to increase token throughput.

- KV cache and prefetching
  - Session cache TTL: 10m; prefetch warm TTL: 30m. We’ll instrument hit rates and target >70% hit for warm sessions.

- Routing policy (implementation detail)
  - Router evaluates each request by: region match -> latency budget remaining -> cost tier -> model compatibility.
  - In overload conditions, router will (1) drop into int8 fallback, then (2) divert to batch endpoint.

Canary + abort criteria (high level)
  - Duration: 48h @5% then 24h @20%.
  - Abort if P95 exceeds 350ms for >15 minutes, or error rate increases by >0.5% absolute.

Next steps:
  - Marissa, can your team run the tuning sprint (profiling, kernel selection, and quant eval) next week?
  - Samira/Alex, please share the 1k labeled validation set and confirm DocuSign flow if procurement needs exact model names.

I attached the proposal; happy to walk through in a quick call.

Cheers,
Jonas
Attachment: inference_profile_proposal.md (markdown stub)
